analysis: Reviewed SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift (base vs head) and the new tests in SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift. The change adds a per-root cache (readableHeaderIdentities, guarded by maintenanceLock) of lstat identities (dev, ino, size, mtime ns, ctime ns) for block files whose header read succeeded. On the next pass an unchanged identity skips readMetadataOnly, but only if fanoutPassesReadChecks(fanout) holds. That check re-runs isSafeModelRoot, pathResolvesToItself, isRealDirectory and the no-follow openDirectoryChain, so symlink and ancestor safety is preserved. Only successes are cached, so a transient read failure cannot pin a block past its TTL; this protects against T-041 retention. The ownership proof (header readability) gates TTL and budget deletion, and it is now stale-able only while the file identity is unchanged. An attacker (same-UID or peripheral controller) could restore mtime but not ctime via utimes, and replacement changes the inode. Residual: a controller that fabricates stat results could keep a corrupted file classified as owned. Impact is deletion of a file already matching the exact owned name grammar under the dedicated root. That is bounded by removeItemIfSafe and the epoch barrier, and it is outside the attested boundary already accepted for operator-selected volumes. The cache is unbounded only by the number of files in the root and is rebuilt every pass, so pruned entries are dropped. The identity is taken before the read, so a concurrent change is re-read next time. The mutation and removal paths (removeOwned, retireActiveEntries, performUnloadedDestructiveChange) are unchanged. The tests cover ctime-only change, replacement, and retry after a failed read. No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation identified. The SSDBlockStore helpers (isSafeModelRoot, pathResolvesToItself, isRealDirectory, SSDNoFollowIO.openDirectoryChain) were not in the supplied source; their visibility and semantics are assumed from the call sites.
